config.title: Type a form state object with field errors

intro.title: Type a form state object with field errors
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple form state manager by creating a TypeScript type for an object that holds form field values and their associated validation errors. You'll learn how to use TypeScript's type system to define the shape of this object, ensuring type safety for both the data and error messages. The core concept involves creating a custom type that uses union types and optional properties to represent fields that may or may not have errors. You'll work with basic TypeScript constructs like type aliases and object types to structure your data model. By the end, you'll have a typed form state object that can help prevent runtime errors in form handling.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for building robust form validation in real applications like user registration forms, checkout processes, and settings panels. In e-commerce sites, it ensures shipping address fields are validated before order submission. In admin dashboards, it validates configuration forms before saving changes. Developers use this approach to provide clear error feedback while maintaining type safety across the entire form lifecycle.

objectives: Construct a TypeScript interface to define a form state object with typed fields
Apply a union type to define possible error states for each form field
Initialize a form state object with default values and error properties
Implement a validation function that updates error states based on field values
Manipulate the form state by handling input changes and error updates
Integrate the typed form state with a simple UI structure to display field errors
Configure a form submission handler that checks the state's validity

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in both React and useState from the 'react' module.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The imports are added at the top of the file, making React and useState available for use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure you import both React and useState from 'react'. Check your import statement syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import React and useState from 'react' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main Form component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named Form that returns a simple JSX element, such as a <div> with a heading.
steps.hint: Define a function called Form that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create a functional component named Form that returns JSX
steps.expectedOutcome: The Form component is defined and returns a JSX element.
successCriteria: A component named Form is defined and returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the Form component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'Form' and returns JSX.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is missing or incorrect. Ensure you create a function named Form that returns JSX.

steps.title: Define the form state interface
steps.instruction: Inside the Form component, define a TypeScript interface named FormState with username, email, and password fields, all typed as strings.
steps.hint: Create an interface using the 'interface' keyword, then list the field names with their types.
steps.expectedOutcome: An interface named FormState with three string fields will be defined inside the component.
successCriteria: The FormState interface is defined with username, email, and password fields, all typed as strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the interface has all three fields (username, email, password) and each is typed as a string.
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface is missing or incorrect. Ensure you define an interface named FormState with username, email, and password as strings.

steps.title: Initialize the form state with useState
steps.instruction: Inside your Form component, call useState to create a state variable named 'formState' with an initial object that matches the FormState interface. Type the state variable and setter using the FormState type.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with an initial object containing empty string values for name and email. Remember to add the type annotation for the state variable.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: typed state initialization
const [user, setUser] = useState<User>({ name: '', age: 0 });
steps.expectedOutcome: The formState variable is properly typed and initialized with empty string values for name and email fields.
successCriteria: formState is declared using useState with the FormState type and initialized with { name: '', email: '' }
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the FormState type and initializing with an object containing name and email fields as empty strings.
steps.feedbackWrong: call useState with an initial FormState object and type the state variable.

steps.title: Initialize the form errors with useState
steps.instruction: In your Form component, call useState to initialize a formErrors state variable with an empty FormErrors object as the initial value.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook with an empty object {} as the initial value, and type it as FormErrors.
steps.expectedOutcome: The formErrors state variable is initialized with an empty FormErrors object using useState.
successCriteria: formErrors is declared using useState with an empty object initial value and typed as FormErrors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with an empty object {} and typing it as FormErrors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The formErrors state isn't properly initialized. Use useState with an empty FormErrors object.

steps.title: Create a form validation handler
steps.instruction: Create a function named validateForm inside your Form component that validates the form state and updates form errors.
steps.hint: Define a function that checks if the name and email fields are filled and sets appropriate error messages.
steps.expectedOutcome: A validateForm function is defined inside the component that validates form fields and sets error messages.
successCriteria: The validateForm function is created and uses the form state to check for empty fields and update form errors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it validates both name and email fields and updates formErrors.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation function isn't quite right. Create a function named validateForm that validates the form state and updates form errors.

steps.title: Add the form structure with input fields
steps.instruction: Inside the Form component's return statement, replace the existing content with a <form> element containing labeled input fields for name and email.
steps.hint: Create a form element with two input fields, each with a label and appropriate type attributes.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: basic form structure
<form>
  <label>
    Username:
    <input type="text" />
  </label>
  <label>
    Email:
    <input type="email" />
  </label>
</form>
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a form element with two labeled input fields for name and email.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a <form> element with two <label> and <input> pairs for name and email fields.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have a <form> element with both name and email fields.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form structure is missing or incomplete. Check that you have a <form> element with labeled inputs for both name and email.

steps.title: Connect inputs to form state with onChange handlers
steps.instruction: Add two input fields inside the form: one for name and one for email. For each input, add an onChange handler that updates the corresponding field in formState using setFormState.
steps.hint: Use the onChange event on each input to call setFormState with the updated value. Remember to spread the previous state to keep other fields unchanged.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have two input fields that update the typed formState when the user types in them.
successCriteria: Two input fields are added with onChange handlers that update formState.name and formState.email respectively.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the inputs, but make sure each has an onChange handler that updates the correct field in formState using setFormState.
steps.feedbackWrong: The inputs are not properly connected to the form state. Add onChange handlers that call setFormState to update the corresponding field.

steps.title: Display validation errors and add submit button
steps.instruction: Inside your Form component, add a submit button to the form structure and display validation error messages below each input field.
steps.hint: Add a <button type='submit'> inside the form. For each field, conditionally render its error message from formErrors if it exists.
steps.expectedOutcome: The form will have a submit button and show typed error messages for invalid fields when validation runs.
successCriteria: A submit button is added to the form. Error messages from formErrors are conditionally rendered below their respective input fields.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but ensure both the submit button and conditional error messages for both name and email fields are present.
steps.feedbackWrong: The form is missing the submit button or error message display. Review the instruction to add these UI elements.
